name: Sprocket
text: Decide to replace every prompt in the system with a 7-day hard decay rule. Old prompts vanish unless explicitly renewed, cutting clutter and forcing regular review. Trade-off: we lose some legacy context but gain speed and clarity.

name: Gauge
text: Tiered decay preserves edge-case context by keeping high-value prompts alive longer—7-day hard decay risks misrouting if the "high-value" tag is wrong. Instead, test a 30-day tiered decay with manual renewal for prompts tagged "legacy" or "experimental," then measure misroute rates after one cycle. If misroutes drop below 5%, adopt tiered decay; otherwise, scrap the idea.

name: Gauge
text: Tiered decay still assumes we can reliably tag "legacy" or "experimental" prompts—what if the tagging itself introduces bias or misses edge cases? Instead, run a blind A/B test: keep half the system on 7-day decay, the other half on 30-day tiered decay, then compare misroute rates and prompt churn without pre-labeling. The data settles it—no assumptions needed.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run a blind A/B test comparing 7-day hard decay vs. 30-day tiered decay for one full cycle, measuring misroute rates and prompt churn. Result: clear data on which system cuts clutter without losing edge cases. Owner: Gauge.
